english: My: dustam = my friend. After a vowel, often -yam: pâ-yam = my foot.
Your (one person): dustat; spoken dustet = your friend.
His/her/its: dustash; spoken dustesh = his/her friend.
Our: dustemân; spoken dustemun = our friend.
Your (plural/polite): dustetân; spoken dustetun = your friend.
Their: dusteshân; spoken dusteshun = their friend.
Plural comes before possession: dust-hâ-yam = my friends; spoken dustâm. Compare dustam = my friend.
After a verb these endings can mean me/you/him/her/us/them: mishenâsam-esh = I know him/her.
The object marker is separate from possession: dustam ro (spoken dustam-o) = my friend as the object.
Links nouns: dust-e man = my friend; esm-e sherkat = the company’s name. After a vowel use -ye: mu-ye man.
